news.title: AI可防御性成为M&A估值的关键因素
news.snippet: [人工智能正深刻改写并购估值逻辑，企业的AI可防御性（技术壁垒、数据优势、规模效应）已成为影响M&A估值与竞争力的关键考量。]
news.raw_snippet:
Artificial intelligence is rewriting the rules of mergers and acquisitions, forcing dealmakers to reconsider what makes businesses valuable. Javi Rodriguez, Global Head of Strategy at KPMG International, explains why AI defensibility is becoming a critical factor in assessing acquisition targets.

Q: Why is AI moving up the M&A agenda?

AI is changing how businesses generate value across software, engineering and professional services. [...] AI assessment needs to begin during acquisition screening rather than appearing as an additional exercise near the end of due diligence.

Buyers should evaluate both opportunities and threats. AI could accelerate growth, improve productivity and strengthen customer relationships. Equally, it could erode revenues, weaken margins or undermine established market positions. [...] Dealmakers therefore need to examine not just current capabilities but management’s capacity to adapt as technological and commercial conditions evolve, even before the transaction is completed.

Ultimately, AI is making competitive advantage more difficult to measure precisely when accurate valuation matters most.

news.title: AI热潮推动全球M&A逼近历史高位：Apollo Sløk
news.snippet: [全球并购交易总值正快速攀升并接近历史最高水平，企业对AI赛道的追逐成为推动M&A市场回暖与交易估值扩张的核心动力。]
news.raw_snippet:
The value of global mergers and acquisitions is soaring close to a record level this year as companies rush to gain a competitive edge from artificial intelligence, according to Apollo Global Management Chief Economist Torsten Sløk. [...] ### Dive Insight:

The fixation on AI has spurred dealmaking well beyond technology into companies involved in sectors essential for the AI build-out, including data centers, power generation, power grid infrastructure, cooling and connectivity, Sløk said.

“AI is the trigger of the AI boom, but it is lighting up far more than tech,” he said, noting that dealmaking involving utilities and energy companies posted a record first half. [...] Among the largest AI-focused deals, SpaceX in June bought Anysphere, the creator of AI-coding agent Cursor, for $55 billion, according to Mergermarket.

Although the value of deals soared during the first nine months of this year, the volume declined by 1% to 32,419 transactions, according to ION Analytics.

news.title: IBM：AI决策模型的新员工测试
news.snippet: [IBM提出应像考核新员工一样评估AI决策模型，重点关注置信度分数、可解释性以及模型在实际业务场景中的稳定表现与持续改进。]
news.raw_snippet:
That’s also why the decision model’s confidence score matters so much. Once a workflow is running, decisions that clear the threshold can be acted on without a person ever seeing them. In a recent IBM Institute for Business Value survey of 2,000 CEOs worldwide, respondents said 25% of operational decisions are currently made by AI, without human intervention. By 2030, leaders expect this to nearly double to 48%. [...] so the two kinds of models serve different, complementary jobs: decision models make the quick calls inside software, and LLMs handle the conversation. [...] By Hannah Press

How many of the decisions that you made today actually needed you?  
   
 A good chunk of the decisions any of us make at work are small, routine choices: which email to answer first, which request can wait and, if you’re me, what time to crack open the second Coke Zero of the day—and yes, that’s a very important work decision. Whatever your routine decisions look like, AI is starting to take them off your plate.

## The first principles guiding our work with AI

Gates Foundation CEO Mark Suzman shares the first principles on artificial intelligence (AI) that will be used to guide the foundation’s use of AI.

By Mark Suzman   CEO, Board Member, Gates Foundation

Rebecca Martey breastfeeds her newborn son, Gerald, at Osu Maternity Home in Accra, Ghana. [...] These are an update to our first principles for AI, published in 2023, building on the same fundamental values and goals that drive the foundation’s work, but adjusted to reflect the significant advances and capabilities in the technology. These principles echo the same commitment to equity and access, local partnership, and accountability to impact that has guided our work from the beginning. We expect to update these principles regularly to keep pace with the evolution of the technology and [...] Today, the rise of artificial intelligence reflects a world that still falls far short when it comes to who benefits. The data it's trained on, the infrastructure that runs it, and the markets that fund it are concentrated in a handful of wealthy countries. This means the people who shape it, benefit from it, and have a say in how it develops are largely the same people who have always been first in line. That is the inequity we are working to change.
